findings.evidence: Fig. 6.2's own rendered labels include "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)", while the caption states "the 2 s line — the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget". Table 4-2 (PDF p. 90, printed p. 66) records "TTFT SLO | 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); p95 ≤ 2 s" and PDF p. 104 (printed p. 80): "The two thresholds are not interchangeable: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to, and any pass/fail judgement on a measured distribution is made against the p95 ceiling, not the budget."
findings.issue: Figure-label vs. book-terminology contradiction: the in-figure annotation labels 2 s as the "TTFT budget", which is exactly the conflation the chapter text and Table 4-2 forbid (budget = 1.2 s; ceiling = 2 s). A reader who takes the figure as the SLO definition will plan against the wrong number and will also mis-apply the "p95 ≤ 2 s" ceiling to TTFT only.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the Fig. 6.2 line as "p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s" (and, if the 1.2 s design budget is drawn, label it separately), so the rendered figure matches the caption and Table 4-2.

findings.evidence: Decode row verdict cell: "bandwidth-bound (25 ms TPOT is a budget; ~21% achieved HBM util at the canonical point — 0.70 TB/s ÷ 3.35 TB/s = 20.9%)"; same row's Resource-tell cell: "high HBM util, low FLOP util"; table footnote: "not verdicts on the canonical 8×H100 host's bandwidth adequacy — under tensor parallelism the 140 GB is sharded, so each GPU only needs ~0.70 TB/s against its own ~3.35 TB/s."
findings.issue: The row is internally contradictory: it issues the verdict 'bandwidth-bound' and prescribes the telemetry tell 'high HBM util' while its own derivation states the canonical operating point achieves only ~21% of peak HBM bandwidth. A kernel at 21% of peak bandwidth cannot simultaneously exhibit the row's 'high HBM util' tell, and the footnote concedes the 5.6-vs-3.35 comparison is 'not verdicts on the canonical host's bandwidth adequacy'. The verdict as printed would send a reader to buy bandwidth the canonical host does not need.
findings.fix_instruction: Restate the verdict cell as a regime classification only ('memory-bound by intensity ~1 FLOP/byte << ridge ~295; weight-read bandwidth not binding at the canonical point'), move the 20.9%-utilization figure into the verdict cell, and relabel the Resource-tell cell as the batch-1 single-device illustration, or delete the tell from this row.

findings.evidence: In-figure annotation: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)"; the same page's caption: "the p95 SLO is met (p95 ≈ 0.99 s ≤ 2 s)" and "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Table 4-2), not the 1.2 s design budget"; Ch 4 (p. 104): "1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling the budget relaxes to".
findings.issue: The figure's axis annotation labels the 2 s line as the 'TTFT budget', but everywhere else in the book 1.2 s is the design budget and 2 s is the p95 ceiling. The in-figure label contradicts the figure's own caption and Table 4-2's terminology, re-conflating the two thresholds the book says are 'not interchangeable'.
findings.fix_instruction: Relabel the annotation to 'p95 TTFT ceiling 2 s' (or 'SLO: p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s') and, if desired, add a separate 1.2 s design-budget marker to the figure.

findings.evidence: "The plotted stream is a synthetic sample of N = 10,000 requests — 99% drawn from a log-normal with median 0.8 s and log-scale dispersion σ ≈ 0.12 (generated as exp(μ + σZ), with μ = ln 0.8 and Z standard normal), 1% a straggler cluster at 5.0 s... The two-point approximation of the mean is E[L] ≈ 0.99 × 0.8 + 0.01 × 5.0 ≈ 0.84 s". Later on the page: "The mean hides the tail; percentiles expose it".
findings.issue: Arithmetic verification: The text calculates the mean as 0.842 s, but also says that the exact mean of the synthetic stream is 0.85 s. While acknowledging the difference, the discrepancy between the analytical mean of the mixture and the exact sample mean is left slightly confusing. Additionally, the text states that 'The population p99 of this 99 % log-normal + 1 % straggler mixture is 5.0 s', which is technically correct (since the stragglers constitute the top 1% and are at exactly 5.0s), but the statement that 'a p95 TTFT-ceiling line drawn on request latency flags a superset of TTFT violations' (page 115) relies on the assumption that Request Latency >= TTFT, which ignores the possibility that Request Latency = TTFT + Generation Time, thus TTFT <= Request Latency. A violation of request latency does not guarantee a TTFT violation.
findings.fix_instruction: Refine the statement on page 115 about the superset of TTFT violations to explicitly note that the p95 TTFT line drawn on request latency is an *upper bound* proxy and not a strict superset, since high request latency can occur without TTFT violations (due to decode phase delays).

findings.evidence: "Hosts were raised from H = 1 to H = 21. That is the capacity floor, which is the max of the named screens, not the prefill compute screen alone: case (i)’s prefill screen needs ⌈18.6⌉ = 19 hosts, but the KV-residency / Little’s-Law screen needs ⌈344/17⌉ = 21 hosts at the peak and therefore binds"
findings.issue: Arithmetic verification: The text correctly computes 344/17 = 20.235, which ceilings to 21. The previous pages establish the 344 in-flight requests based on a peak arrival rate of 40 rps and a service time of 8.6s. The prefill screen uses 18.6 host-equivalents. The logic is sound.
findings.fix_instruction: No action needed; this calculation verifies correctly against the stated parameters.
